questions.stemHtml: A child presents with lesions on the trunk and inner thigh as shown in the figure. It initially started as a macule and later developed into nodules, few of which have central umbilication. Which of the following will be seen in histopathology?
questions.solutionHtml:
Henderson Paterson bodies
  • The given clinical scenario and histological image are diagnostic of molluscum contagiosum lesions, which show intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies, called Henderson-Patterson bodies or molluscum bodies.


Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 342

questions.stemHtml: A 10 year old boy noticed the passage of a white thread like worm in stool. Microscopic examination of the anterior end of the worm is shown in the figure. The segments of the worm had breadth greater than length. Which of the following eggs would be likely seen in stool? Choose the correct answer from below given options:
questions.solutionHtml:
1
  • Presence of segments suggest the parasite as cestode. Image shows it to be armed and broad segments suggesting it to be H nana.
  • Diagnosis is usually made by looking at typical non bile stained eggs with 3 pairs of Hooksett, polar filaments and yolk granules.



Ananthanaryan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page 197

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following viruses exhibits genetic reassortment similar to that of the influenza virus?
questions.solutionHtml:
1
  • 1 –is having a segmented genome & hence can show reassortment.
  • Genetic Reassortment is the process by which influenza viruses swap gene segments.
  • This genetic exchange is possible due to the segmented nature of the viral genome

Option A

  • Rotavirus
  • Hence option 1 is the correct answer

Option B

  • Adenovirus is not segmented
  • Hence option B is not correct option

Option C

  • Ebola virus not segmented
  • Hence option C is not correct option

Option D Rabies virus

  • Not segmented
  • Hence option D is not correct option






Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 652

questions.stem: Which of the following cytokines are not Involved in a TH2 response?
questions.solutionHtml:
IL 12
  • Cytokines are proteins produced by many cell types (principally activated lymphocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells, but also endothelial, epithelial, and connective tissue cells) that mediate and regulate immune and inflammatory reactions.
  • Three subsets of CD4- T cells secrete different types of cytokines and elicit different types of inflammation.
  • TH1 cells - activate macrophages by the classical pathway by secreting IFNy
  • TH2 cells - recruit and activate eosinophils and are responsible for the alternative pathway of macrophage activation by secreting IL4, IL5, and IL13
    • IL4 acts on B cells to stimulate class switching to lgE and promotes the development of additional TH2 cells.
    • IL5 is involved in the development and activation of eosinophils, which are essential effectors of type I hypersensitivity (discussed later).
    • IL13 enhances IgE production and acts on epithelial cells to stimulate mucus secretion
  • TH17 cells secrete IL17 and other cytokines responsible for neutrophils and monocyte recruitment. 

Cytokines produced

IFN-Y

IL-4, IL-5, IL-13

IL-17, IL-22

questions.topic: eGurukul · Microbiology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.stemHtml: An HIV positive male with a CD4 count of 145/cumm reports to the OPD with complaints of severe watery diarrhoea for the last 3 days. Acid fast stain of a stool sample demonstrated acid fast round the size of 4-6 microns. Which of the following is the likely etiology of the symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cryptosporidium Hominis
  • Cryptosporidiosis is caused by various species of the protozoan parasite Cryptosporidium, which infects the small bowel mucosa, and, if symptomatic, the infection typically causes diarrhoea.
  • Advanced immunosuppression—typically CD4 T lymphocyte cell (CD4) counts <100 cells/mm3—is associated with the greatest risk for prolonged, severe, or extraintestinal cryptosporidiosis
  • Diagnosis of cryptosporidiosis was traditionally made by microscopic identification of the oocysts in stool with acid-fast staining or direct immunofluorescence, which offers higher sensitivity. Concentration methods (e.g., formalin-ethyl acetate) may facilitate diagnosis of cryptosporidiosis.
  • Isospora belli : Cystoisospora belli, previously known as Isospora belli, is a parasite that causes an intestinal disease known as Cysto isosporiasis
  • Cyclospora is a genus of apicomplexan parasites.
  • It includes the species Cyclospora cayetanensis, the causative agent of cyclosporiasis.
  • Members of Cyclospora are characterized as having oocysts with two sporocysts, each containing two sporozoites




Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 1423

questions.stem: Microscopy technique that can be utilised to produce high- contrast images of transparent specimens, such as living cells, is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Phase Contrast Microscopy
  • Phase-contrast microscopy is an optical microscopy technique that converts phase shifts in light passing through a transparent specimen to brightness changes in the image.
  • Phase shifts themselves are invisible, but become visible when shown as brightness variations



Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 42

questions.stemHtml: A microbiologist performed a tissue gram stain and found thin, filamentous bacteria shown in the figure. What other staining technique should be done to confirm the diagnosis as Nocardia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Modified Acid Fast Stain
  • Nocardia is typically weakly acid-fast after traditional carbol-fuchsin staining and positive on modified acid-fast staining (1%) due to the presence of mycolic acid in the cell wall. Unlike mycobacteria (also acid-fast positive), Nocardia has a FILAMENTOUS, ELONGATED, BRANCHING  appearance on acid-fast staining.



Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 312

questions.stemHtml: Peripheral blood smear in a patient presenting with fever, headache and malaise showed rickettsial morulae in GRANULOCYTES. Which of the following is the likely cause of the symptoms in the patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anaplasma Phagocytophilum
  • Anaplasma phagocytophilum is an obligate gram-negative, intracellular bacterium that causes an acute febrile illness known as anaplasmosis or human granulocytic anaplasmosis (HGA)


Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 851

questions.stemHtml: Acid fast stain of a specimen showed the following microscopic appearance. Which of the following is the likely organism seen in the specimen?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nocardia Brasiliensis
  • The image showing filamentous, branching acid-fast rods is suggestive of Nocardia. Nocardia appears as filamentous organisms with extensive hyphae-like branching.
  • They are gram-positive, catalase-positive, and produce urease. They are weakly acid-fast (1% acid fast)


Ananthanaryan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 399

questions.stem: Petechial rash is associated with all the following except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Roseola Infantum
  • Roseola infantum is caused by infection with human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6), or, less frequently, by human herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7).
  • Roseola infantum, also known as exanthema subitum or sixth disease, typically presents in children between six and 12 months of age
  • Patients with the virus classically present with acute onset high-grade fever up to 40 degrees celsius (104 degrees fahrenheit) lasting between three and five days.
  • After that, rapid defervescence of the fever is accompanied by a nonpruritic, pink papular rash that begins on the trunk.
  • Clinically diagnosed, self-limited illness that can be treated symptomatically
  • The causative agents of Zika, Kyasanur Forest disease, and West Nile fever belong to the Flaviviridae group of viruses, which are known to cause hemorrhagic fever and present with petechial rashes.


Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 148

questions.stem: Transmission of which of the following viral Disease has been reported in India -
questions.solutionHtml:
West Nile Fever
  • West Nile virus is a flavivirus that is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes. It can be subclinical or may present as a mild influenza-like illness. Encephalitis occurs in severe forms. Reverse-transcriptase PC has been used to identify the virus
  • Hendra virus is endemic to Australia, and mostly affects horses.
  • Ebola virus belongs to the genus Filovirus. It causes hemorrhagic fever. It is endemic to Africa.
  • Yellow fever is mostly confined to South and Central America, and certain parts of Africa. It is caused by flavivirus. It is an arthropod-borne hemorrhagic fever. Aedes aegypti transmits the disease.


Ananthanaryan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology, 10th Edition, Page No. 528
